title: Hash-key dedup (exact duplicates)
symptom: nested loop comparing rows; x in list inside a loop; list.count inside a loop; dedup is slow; removing duplicates takes hours
precondition: a hashable key(row) exists such that same(a, b) == (key(a) == key(b)), property-tested on random pairs
reject_when: equality is fuzzy or context dependent (use Blocking for near-duplicates)
data already sorted by the key and memory is tight (use Sort then scan)
complexity: O(n^2) comparisons -> O(n) expected hashing, O(n) extra memory
oracle: nested-loop keep-first on 0..60 rows, 300 seeded cases with case, whitespace, Unicode form, 1.0 vs 1, negative timestamps and NaN

title: Dict index join
symptom: nested loop join on an id or foreign key; a lookup list searched once per row
precondition: the join condition is equality on one or a few fields and one side fits in memory as a dict
reject_when: the condition is a range or inequality (use Sort then scan)
both sides are already in a database (write the join in SQL)
complexity: O(n*m) -> O(n + m) expected
oracle: nested loop on 0..40 rows per side, 300 cases, duplicate keys on both sides and mixed key types ('42' vs 42)

title: Sort then scan
symptom: range or interval join; dedup or grouping under tight memory; sorted output wanted
precondition: a total order on the key exists and comparing two keys is cheap (no mixed int and str keys)
reject_when: a hashable key exists and memory is fine (Hash-key dedup is simpler)
complexity: O(n^2) -> O(n log n), O(1) extra memory beyond the sort
oracle: nested loop on small inputs; equal multisets, and equal sequences when order matters

title: Blocking for near-duplicates
symptom: records that are the same despite typos, spacing or formatting; fuzzy similarity over all pairs
precondition: exact canonicalisation done first, and a cheap blocking key that true duplicates almost always share exists
reject_when: n <= about 3,000 (run full pairwise once)
exact equality after canonicalisation is enough (Hash-key dedup)
complexity: O(n^2) -> O(sum of block sizes squared), O(n*b) with largest block b
oracle: full pairwise similarity on a sample that contains labelled duplicate pairs; report recall and the pair count it rests on

title: Prefix sums and sliding window
symptom: rolling or windowed aggregate recomputed per window; sum or max of a[i:i+w] for every i; events in the last 5 minutes per event
precondition: the aggregate is invertible (sum, count), min or max, a distinct count, or defined on a sorted axis
reject_when: the aggregate is a median or percentile
complexity: O(n*w) -> O(n)
oracle: recompute each window from scratch on arrays of 0..50 elements, every window width

title: Reverse-graph impact set
symptom: which services, modules or tests are affected if X changes; what depends on this; closure recomputed per node
precondition: all edges enumerable from a source of truth, with the missed edge kinds named and the consumer able to fail closed on them
reject_when: the graph cannot be made complete and the consumer cannot fail closed
V is tiny and the time is spent fetching the graph (cache the fetch)
complexity: O(V*(V+E)) or worse -> O(V+E) per query
oracle: transitive closure by Floyd-Warshall on random graphs with V <= 30, cycles and self-loops, every start node
facts: O(V+E) per query (BFS on the reversed graph)

title: SCC condensation
symptom: many reachability queries on a graph with cycles; groups that depend on each other for release order
precondition: cycles exist and queries are many
reject_when: the graph is a DAG (Topological order)
one query (Reverse-graph impact set)
complexity: O(V+E) once, then queries on a smaller DAG
oracle: brute-force mutual reachability on V <= 25 graphs; equivalence classes equal the SCCs

title: Bitset closure for many queries
symptom: thousands of does-a-reach-b queries per run on a DAG
precondition: V <= about 20,000 (V^2/8 bytes) and queries per rebuild far exceed V
reject_when: few queries (per-query BFS)
V above the memory bound
complexity: O(V*E/64) word operations to build; O(1) per query on frozen byte rows
oracle: per-query BFS on random DAGs with V <= 60, every (a, b) pair

title: Topological order and cycle detection
symptom: build order, migration order, run in dependency order, is there a cycle
precondition: edges are known and an order is needed, not a schedule across workers
reject_when: makespan on m workers is the question (Critical-path list scheduling)
complexity: O(V+E) with a sorted ready set
oracle: every edge satisfied on random DAGs with V <= 40; one injected back edge reported as a cycle

title: Union-find for grouping
symptom: merge records that are linked; connected components done by repeated list merging
precondition: the relation is symmetric (undirected)
reject_when: edges are directed
complexity: O(n^2) list merging -> near O(n)
oracle: BFS components on random undirected graphs with n <= 50

title: Impact-based test selection
symptom: every PR runs the full test suite; which tests actually need to run for this PR
precondition: a test-to-source graph from the checkout, a sensitive-file list, an ignore list, and a scheduled full run to catch escapes
reject_when: the graph cannot be produced from the checkout
the suite is under about 5 minutes
no scheduled full run exists
complexity: full suite every PR -> O(V+E) selection plus the selected subset
oracle: escapes against full-run results on the last k merged commits (target 0) and the selection ratio; reverse BFS property test

title: Content-hash cache (skip unchanged steps)
symptom: a build, lint, codegen or image step reruns on unchanged inputs every time
precondition: the step is deterministic given an enumerable input set: files, tool version, flags, environment variables it reads
reject_when: the step is a small share of wall time
the step is not deterministic
complexity: cost(step) every run -> cost(hash inputs) on a hit
oracle: cache disabled on a sample of commits; outputs compared byte for byte

title: Coverage under a time budget
symptom: fixed CI time budget; choose optional suites or checks; pick the exact best set in B minutes
precondition: mandatory items excluded and subtracted from B first, durations measured (p50), value additive or overlapping decided
reject_when: there is no real budget
value cannot be estimated (select by impact only)
complexity: additive: 0/1 knapsack O(n*B); overlapping: greedy plus best single; exact search only for n <= 18 under a node budget
oracle: brute force over all subsets for n <= 12: DP exact, greedy >= 0.31 x optimum; exact search at the cutoff finishes, past it returns None

title: LPT across workers
symptom: CI takes 40 minutes on several runners; uneven jobs split alphabetically or round-robin; wall time far above total over runners
precondition: m >= 2, independent jobs, measured p50 durations validated, current plan replayed within about 10% of observed
reject_when: jobs have dependencies (Critical-path list scheduling)
the longest job exceeds sum/m
makespan already within 10% of LB
complexity: O(n log n) with a heap; makespan <= (4/3 - 1/(3m)) x optimal
oracle: brute force all m^n assignments for n <= 8, m <= 3: every job once, bound holds, deterministic

title: Critical path
symptom: pipeline of stages takes 25 minutes when most stages take 2; which stage should we shorten
precondition: a DAG of stages with measured durations; a cycle is reported first
reject_when: no dependencies (LPT across workers)
complexity: O(V+E) dynamic programming in topological order
oracle: all paths enumerated on DAGs with V <= 12 including zero-duration stages and ties; the returned path is real and sums to the length

title: Critical-path list scheduling
symptom: dependent jobs on several workers; a build graph on a pool of agents
precondition: DAG, m >= 2, durations known
reject_when: no dependencies (LPT is simpler with a better bound)
complexity: O(n log n + E); within (2 - 1/m) of optimal
oracle: brute force on n <= 7, m = 2: feasibility and the bound

title: Fewest workers for a deadline
symptom: how many runners do we need to finish in D minutes
precondition: every job's duration <= D and jobs are independent
reject_when: m is fixed (use LPT and report the makespan)
complexity: first-fit decreasing, O(n log n) with a tree; at most 11/9 OPT + 6/9 bins
oracle: brute-force minimum bins for n <= 8; a job longer than D raises

title: Aho-Corasick for literal patterns
symptom: thousands of literal patterns checked per log line; for p in patterns: if p in line
precondition: patterns are literals, k >= 50, text far longer than the patterns, pattern set fixed for many lines
reject_when: k < 50 (a loop or one compiled alternation is fine)
patterns change on every call
the patterns are true regexes
complexity: O(L*k) -> O(L + P + z)
oracle: per-pattern str.find (all occurrences) on 2000 sampled lines; sorted match sets equal

title: Literal prefilter for regex sets
symptom: hundreds or thousands of regexes run on every line
precondition: a required literal can be extracted from each regex and the always-run set is under 20% of k
reject_when: 20% or more of the regexes have no required literal (Combined alternation)
complexity: O(L*k*c) -> O(L + hits*c + L*a)
oracle: all k regexes on 2000 sampled lines plus crafted lines and 50 generated matching strings per regex; match sets equal

title: Combined alternation on a linear-time engine
symptom: many regexes without usable literals checked per line
precondition: a linear-time engine (RE2, Go regexp, Rust regex, Hyperscan) is available and allowed
reject_when: the platform cannot take the dependency and the always-run set is small (Literal prefilter is enough)
complexity: O(L*k) -> O(L) per line for the DFA
oracle: the full k-regex loop on 2000 sampled lines; equal match sets

title: Exact-first retrieval
symptom: the context packer misses the file the task literally names; embeddings retrieve the wrong files
precondition: the task text names identifiers, paths, error strings or commands
reject_when: the task has no concrete names (Sparse scoring)
complexity: O(repo size) with a fast searcher, once per task
oracle: recall 1.0 on labelled tasks for files whose path or defining symbol the task names

title: Sparse scoring (BM25) over chunks
symptom: ranking candidate chunks by relevance offline; results must be the same every run
precondition: text tokenises into terms and chunks are defined; at least about 200 chunks
reject_when: fewer than about 200 chunks (score them all directly)
complexity: index O(total tokens) once; query O(query terms x postings)
oracle: direct scoring with the same formula; top-k and scores equal to 1e-9 on 100 queries over 500 chunks

title: Bounded graph expansion
symptom: the packer loads the whole repo map or nothing; callers and callees of the named targets are needed
precondition: a symbol or import graph exists and a hop cap and node cap are chosen before expansion
reject_when: no graph
the direct targets already fill the budget
complexity: whole repo map O(V) -> O(nodes within k hops, capped)
oracle: unbounded BFS truncated by the same caps on small graphs

title: Pack under a token budget
symptom: LLM prompt over the token budget; context packer truncates and drops the test command or constraints
precondition: a token estimate per chunk, the must-keep set identified, and a budget B
reject_when: everything relevant fits (include it all, in fixed order)
complexity: O(c log c + c x k log k) for c candidates and k must-keep ranges
oracle: must-keep always present; total <= B or the over-budget note; no line sent twice; >= half the knapsack optimum on 200 instances with c <= 12; fixed order

title: Memoise pure functions
symptom: a function called many times with few distinct arguments: parsing the same config, resolving the same path
precondition: the function is pure and its arguments are hashable or reducible to a hashable key
reject_when: distinct inputs nearly as many as calls
the function is cheap
complexity: calls x cost -> distinct x cost + calls x O(1)
oracle: cached and uncached on the same call sequence, including a caller that mutates what it receives

title: Content-hash cache across runs
symptom: a build or data step reruns for all inputs although few changed
precondition: the step's inputs are enumerable and the step is deterministic given them
reject_when: the step is nondeterministic and cannot be fixed
the step is cheap
complexity: cost(all) every run -> cost(changed) + hashing
oracle: periodic full recompute with the cache disabled; report the hit rate

title: Incremental recompute via dependents
symptom: outputs depend on other items, so per-item caching is not enough; everything recomputes when one input changes
precondition: a complete dependency graph among items, failing closed on edge kinds it misses
reject_when: items are independent (Content-hash cache across runs)
complexity: recompute all -> recompute the impact set of the changed items
oracle: full recompute against incremental on random change sets with deletions and additions

title: Index once, query many
symptom: each query scans the full data; linear search or re-reading a file per lookup
precondition: queries per rebuild x per-query saving exceed the build cost; data changes less often than it is queried
reject_when: fewer than about 10 queries per rebuild
the data changes on every query
complexity: O(n) per query -> O(log n) or O(1), plus an O(n log n) build
oracle: linear scan per query on random data

title: Coalesce identical requests
symptom: N identical fetches or computations issued concurrently or within a short window
precondition: requests are identical by key and the result can be shared within the window
reject_when: results are user-specific and the key cannot include the user
complexity: N x cost -> 1 x cost + N x O(1)
oracle: backend calls counted under threads with repeated keys: one per distinct key per window
